name: Aviation
description: Flight from the first balloons and the Wright brothers to the jumbo jet, Concorde and the A380.

checkpoints.name: Balloons and airships
checkpoints.note: Balloons lift the first aeronauts in 1783, and rigid airships follow. For more than a century flight means floating, not flying.

checkpoints.name: The first aeroplanes
checkpoints.note: The Wrights fly at Kitty Hawk, Blériot crosses the Channel, and the First World War turns the aeroplane from a curiosity into a weapon.

checkpoints.name: Record flights and airliners
checkpoints.note: Lindbergh crosses the Atlantic alone, Earhart becomes a star, the DC-3 makes airlines pay, and the Hindenburg fire ends the passenger airship.

checkpoints.name: War and the jet engine
checkpoints.note: The Second World War brings radar, long-range bombers, the first jet aircraft and the first practical helicopter. After it, jets begin to carry passengers, with early troubles.

checkpoints.name: Jumbo jets and Concorde
checkpoints.note: Jet airliners shrink the globe. The 747 brings low fares, Concorde crosses the Atlantic at twice the speed of sound, and military aircraft fly faster than ever.

checkpoints.name: Modern airliners
checkpoints.note: Airbus and Boeing build bigger or more efficient aircraft. The A380 and An-225 are the giants of the air, but twin-engine jets win the market.
